chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Yazid ibn Farqad, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-suht (forbidden earnings). So he said: It is bribery in judgment.

key_terms.الرِّشَا: Al-risha: bribery, the act of offering or accepting payment to influence a decision
key_terms.السُّحْت: Al-suht: forbidden/illicit earnings, a Quranic term (Q5:42, Q5:62) for categorically prohibited income
key_terms.الْحُكْم: Al-hukm: judgment, judicial ruling, legal decision

ai.seo_question: What is al-suht (forbidden earnings) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Yazid ibn Farqad asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about al-suht, a Quranic term for illicit or forbidden earnings. The Imam gave a precise jurisprudential definition: al-suht specifically refers to bribery in the context of judicial rulings. This hadith establishes that accepting bribes to influence legal judgments is among the gravest categories of forbidden income in Islamic law.
